problems.what: The noun 'rent' (the monthly money paid for a home). Only the act root rent [A] exists; rent.made would be the rented thing, and 'price KIND rent' is two words that then need brackets every time they are modified.
problems.workaround: Defined spare word 1 as 'money KIND { pay AGENT rent.doer THEME SELF TO own.doer PER month }' and used it throughout.

problems.what: 'tenant' and 'landlord' as plain words
problems.workaround: Built rent.doer (not in derived list, by rule) and used listed own.doer; then handles. own.doer does not say owner of what.

problems.what: A currency unit (euro) and a general way to say an amount of money
problems.workaround: Wrote numbers with «EUR» in notation, e.g. 950 «EUR»; also used a bare '890 «EUR»' as a THEME phrase with no head root, unsure the checker accepts number+notation as a full phrase.

problems.what: A calendar date: '1 March', '1 June'. The sheet says months are NAME + loan but gives no pattern for day-of-month.
problems.workaround: Wrote 'WHEN ORD 1 day OF NAME ~march' (and ~june). Also used a bare 'NAME ~june' as the REL term of 'before'.

problems.what: 'starting from / as of 1 March' (an onset that then continues). FROM was already needed for the old amount (from 850 to 950), and WHEN is only a point in time.
problems.workaround: Used WHEN + date, which reads as the increase happening on that day.

problems.what: 'No further increase for the two years after that' and 'only one year, not two'
problems.workaround: 'NOT AGAIN increase ... SPAN 2 year WHEN before.opp REL THAT day', and the reply as a fragment 'SPAN ONLY 1 year'. Scope of NOT AGAIN over the SPAN phrase is not obvious.

problems.what: Whether PLAN/REQUEST defaults ('missing AGENT is the writer/addressee') follow the BY speaker in dialogue turns. The sheet says ME shifts inside a BY block but says nothing about the PLAN default for a BY-headed sentence.
problems.workaround: Left AGENT out in PLAN sentences by the landlord (3, 28, 32), assuming writer = BY speaker; added explicit AGENT in PROPOSE sentences to be safe.

problems.what: SOCIAL opener with CALL: 'a bare root follows' vs header order where CALL comes before the body. Also whether SOCIAL may take a participant (apologise for what, agree to what).
problems.workaround: Wrote 'SOCIAL CALL A greet' and kept apology/thanks/agreement as bare roots, putting the content in a separate CLAIM sentence.

problems.what: Farewell / closing a deal ('deal', 'goodbye')
problems.workaround: Ended with 'SOCIAL thank' and 'SOCIAL agree'.

problems.what: 'An increase of 100 euro' and 'too low' for a sum of money
problems.workaround: 'increase KIND 100 «EUR»' (KIND as content/size) and 'TOO big.opp THEME 890 «EUR»'; there is no low/high for amounts distinct from physical size.

problems.what: A veiled threat: 'I would not like to have to look elsewhere'. Hedged, indirect modality (would hate to, might have to) is hard; the explicit opener/strength system pushes everything toward plain assertion.
problems.workaround: Two flat statements: cheaper available homes exist; 'I do not want to leave this home, but I must count my money'.

problems.what: Quoting the other speaker's earlier words: inside the quote the original used ME, and the quote block needs BY + the original speaker so ME resolves correctly even though the quoter is addressing that person as YOU.
problems.workaround: 'PAST say AGENT YOU THEME { BY A GIVEN ... OF ME ... }' - works, but I repeated the whole earlier sentence since there is no 'you said STEP 7' form I was sure of (say THEME STEP n might be valid but would not be a verbatim quote).

problems.what: Referring to an earlier proposal as the object of accept/misunderstand: is 'THEME STEP 18' (a whole sentence as participant) allowed, and may two STEPs be joined with AND?
problems.workaround: Used 'accept AGENT YOU THEME STEP 18', 'understand.opp AGENT ME THEME STEP 9' and 'THEME STEP 22 AND STEP 25'.

problems.what: Every modifier attaches to the head, so 'increase OF price KIND rent' silently mis-attaches; easy to get wrong and it forces brackets for any two-word noun. Also unclear whether a NAMED handle may sit between head and later OF modifier.
problems.workaround: Avoided by the spare word; wrote 'window NAMED G OF cook.place' following the section 5 template.

problems.what: Costs of upkeep ('maintenance costs and taxes rose')
problems.workaround: 'increase THEME tax AND ( price KIND maintain )' - act root used as a KIND modifier of price; unsure it reads as 'cost of maintenance'.

problems.what: tenant / landlord as role nouns
problems.workaround: Gave both people loan names (Ana, Ben) and stated 'Ana rents house H' / 'Ben owns house H'; rent.doer (쿠국일) would be ambiguous between payer and letter, and there is no 'let out' root

problems.what: 'rent' as the monthly sum of money
problems.workaround: ( 조롭 라 쿠국 ) price KIND rent, with 쎠 페린 (PER month) as a clause participant

problems.what: currency unit (euro)
problems.workaround: Treated it as a unit in notation: 1200 «EUR»

problems.what: month names (March, June, August, September) and calendar dates
problems.workaround: NAME + letter-by-letter loans (루거너머, 제티, 우에베허쩌, 히뻐찌러키거) inside ( 너 1 츠킁 래 처 ... ) = 1st day OF March; long and clumsy for a common thing

problems.what: 'starting from date X' (from 1 March on)
problems.workaround: Used FROM (서) with the date phrase; FROM is defined as 'origin', and it is unclear if it covers time starting points or whether WHEN + BEGIN was intended

problems.what: 'X is at most 1000 / not more than 1000' in ordinary (non-logic) prose; MORE as a bare predicate is only shown in logic
problems.workaround: Recast as cost (구둥) THEME the houses SWAP ( 뇨 1000 «EUR» ) PER month, using SWAP as 'price paid'

problems.what: Strength (maybe) inside an IF consequent block for the veiled threat
problems.workaround: Put POSSIBLE in the outer header and used CAN inside the block: 'maybe, if the rent rises to 1200, I can look for another house'

problems.what: Marking a threat as veiled/indirect
problems.workaround: No attitude for 'implied/hinting'; relied on POSSIBLE + CAN wording; the veiledness is not visible to a reader of the script

problems.what: 'I only said X' with ONLY applied to a STEP reference
problems.workaround: 새 파 츠 13 (THEME ONLY STEP 13); unclear whether focus words may precede STEP

problems.what: Goodbye / farewell
problems.workaround: SOCIAL greet (깨 쎄흘) used for both hello and goodbye

problems.what: 'increase by 20 percent'
problems.workaround: SPAN ( 20 르님 ) as size of difference; works but the 'percent' root is glossed oddly ('noun: percent')

problems.what: Speaker in a dialogue stating contract terms (a rule laid down by the contract they are making)
problems.workaround: Used RULE opener with DETAIL 33 pointing at 'I write a contract'; unclear whether RULE is appropriate inside a BY turn for a rule not yet in force

problems.what: yeast
problems.workaround: Defined a spare word as 'fungus that causes the dough to rise' (sentence 2)

problems.what: dough
problems.workaround: Defined a spare word as 'mixture of flour and water' (sentence 1)

problems.what: knead
problems.workaround: Defined a spare word as a bare block 'press many times with the hand and fold many times' (sentence 3); unsure a bare { } block is a legal definition body for an act

problems.what: millilitre (only litre exists, no prefixes or decimals described)
problems.workaround: Wrote 350 «ml» as notation unit

problems.what: degrees Celsius (root 'degree' exists but no way to say which scale)
problems.workaround: Wrote 220 «°C» and 40 «°C» in notation instead of using the degree root

problems.what: Measured quantity of a substance: '500 grams of flour'
problems.workaround: Used unit as head with KIND: '500 gram KIND flour', wrapped each in brackets. Sheet never shows whether it should be this, 'flour SPAN 500 gram', OF, or NOTE; also unclear whether a «unit» can be a phrase head taking KIND

problems.what: 'Repeat until condition holds' in ordinary prose (knead until smooth)
problems.workaround: Used WHILE { NOT smooth THEME dough } { knead THEME dough } after REQUEST SEQUENCE; WHILE is only shown in logic definitions, and there is no 'until' particle

problems.what: A relation meaning 'at the same time as step N' between numbered sentences
problems.workaround: Used ADD + label plus an ALONG { } block restating the other event ('while the yeast dissolves', 'while the dough rises')

problems.what: Imperative with a quality/event root: 'heat the oven', 'make the dough round', 'dissolve the yeast', 'pour the water'
problems.workaround: Wrote AGENT YOU explicitly each time, since with the AGENT omitted in a REQUEST it is unclear whether the causative reading is triggered or it reads 'be hot'

problems.what: 'Twice as big as at the start of the step' (comparison against the same thing at another time)
problems.workaround: 2 EQUAL big THEME dough THAN WHEN ( beginning REL STEP 10 ), relying on 'a role particle may follow THAN'; not sure a time role works there

problems.what: '30 more minutes' / 'another 5 minutes'
problems.workaround: '30 minute KIND extra'; unclear whether OTHER + number would be accepted or mean that

problems.what: 'before cutting the bread' — REL followed by an event with its own object
problems.workaround: before REL ( cut OF bread ) with brackets; sheet does not say whether REL can take a { } block

problems.what: Scope of NOT over a trailing CAUSE block in a prohibition ('do not use hot water, because it kills the yeast')
problems.workaround: Left the CAUSE block at the end of the negated clause; by the 'applies to everything on its right' rule the reason may be read as inside the negation

problems.what: Marking a sentence as a warning (no warning opener/attitude)
problems.workaround: Heading '2 warn.made' plus REQUEST EMPHASIS NOT ...

problems.what: 'If the dough still has not risen, start over with fresh yeast' and 'check again' (referring to a range of steps and to the sentence itself)
problems.workaround: 'AGAIN do THEME STEP 5 UPTO 10 WITH yeast KIND new' and, inside sentence 18, 'AGAIN do THEME STEP 18' (self-reference)

problems.what: baking tray; ingredients; 'sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom'
problems.workaround: 'board KIND metal'; 'material OF bread'; 'if you strike the bottom of the bread and as a result you hear a hollow sound'

problems.what: yeast
problems.workaround: Loan spelled by the letter table, 아이우허쩌. The list has no root for it, and mushroom KIND small would be misleading.

problems.what: dough
problems.workaround: Defined spare 사붕 as mix.made KIND (flour AND water AND salt AND yeast AND oil). The spare shows up in a lot of sentences.

problems.what: knead
problems.workaround: Wrote press THEME dough WITH hand ANDC SEQUENCE fold THEME dough inside the WHILE loop, with no single verb.

problems.what: millilitre and degree Celsius as units
problems.workaround: Used «ml» and «°C» in notation. Gram (새믁) and minute (쏘섭) are roots, and the degree root 커캇 does not say which scale.

problems.what: Quantity plus substance, e.g. '500 g of flour'. The sheet never says how a measured amount combines with a mass noun.
problems.workaround: 500 gram KIND flour (500 새믁 라 쭈좃엄), with the number and unit as head and the substance after KIND. Then 'warm water' needed nested brackets: 350 «ml» KIND ( water KIND ( SLIGHT hot ) ).

problems.what: Does KIND bind tighter than AND in a list of ingredients?
problems.workaround: Put every ingredient in its own brackets inside a NOTE list.

problems.what: Can WHILE open a REQUEST body directly ('keep doing X until Y')? Does the 'missing AGENT = addressee' default reach inside the blocks?
problems.workaround: Wrote 규 도 추 {...} {...} and added AGENT YOU explicitly in every inner clause.

problems.what: Until the dough has doubled in size
problems.workaround: Captured the starting size with logic assignment DEFINE 각 BE ( size OF dough ), then looped WHILE { LESS FIRST (size OF dough) SECOND (multiply 2 각) } { wait }. It works but reads like code, not like a recipe.

problems.what: Spare-word definition for an act. A KIND block with SELF makes SELF the act itself, not the doer.
problems.workaround: Avoided an act spare and defined only a thing spare (dough).

problems.what: 'This takes about 10 minutes' for a looped step
problems.workaround: CLAIM HABIT continue THEME STEP 6 SPAN AROUND 10 minute. Using STEP as the theme of continue is not clearly sanctioned.

problems.what: Strength particles (LIKELY) are header-only, so I could not say 'probably' inside the then-branch of an IF
problems.workaround: Put LIKELY in the header over the whole IF sentence (sentence 21).

problems.what: baking tray, thermometer, warm
problems.workaround: board KIND metal; 'measure the heat of the water' with no instrument named; warm = SLIGHT hot.

problems.what: Refer to 'the member who did X' inside the same rule, i.e. a generic member who is both the agent of the rule and of an embedded time clause ('a member must clean the common area after he has used it')
problems.workaround: Bound a handle to a generic 'any member' (묘 사붕 차 낙) and re-bound the same handle in several rules. SELF could not be used because inside a non-KIND block SELF means the AGENT of that block itself, not of the outer clause.

problems.what: 'After X' with a clause or event as the second term: REL is a linker and the rule only lets roles (not linkers) take a { } block
problems.workaround: Used WHEN { PAST use ... } for 'after using', and 'before REL ( leave OF handle ) SPAN ATLEAST 30 day' for 'at least 30 days before leaving'. The second is awkward, and it is unclear whether SPAN can give the size of a difference on a before-relation.

problems.what: Clock times or opening hours ('from 08:00 to 20:00'), and a date range for how long the contract is valid
problems.workaround: Put the times and dates in notation (SPAN «08:00-20:00», WHEN «2027-01-01»). UPTO is defined only for numbers and labels, so I did not use it with dates.

problems.what: Currency ('300 euros')
problems.workaround: 300 «EUR». A number plus notation as the head of a THEME phrase, modelled on 30 «km/h».

problems.what: Weekday / working day, weekend, smoking
problems.workaround: DEFINE'd a spare word: 거뭄 = a day that is not a holiday (it does not cover weekends). For 'smoke' I used 'use tobacco' (제볼 ... 체칼).

problems.what: Mark an exception to an earlier rule, or say that one rule overrides another
problems.workaround: Used the CONTRAST relation with the label (교 다 6 ..., 교 다 11 ...). No relation particle means 'exception to' or 'overrides'.

problems.what: 'If a member does not meet the payment rule' (referring to a rule as something that is followed or broken)
problems.workaround: 'NOT do THEME STEP 8' (하 깨춘 ... 새 츠 8). It is unclear whether STEP can be the THEME of 'do'.

problems.what: 'Late fee of 20 EUR per day late'
problems.workaround: 20 «EUR» PER day KIND late.opp (쎠 츠킁 라 라둣안): 'per late day', which is loose.

problems.what: 'Two rules conflict; the more specific one wins; if neither is more specific, the manager decides which applies'
problems.workaround: Bound handles to two rules inside an IF block, used contradict = 쿠팜안 with REL, 'MORE general.opp' for 'more specific', 'must follow ONLY 국' for 'wins', and an embedded ASK block for 'decides which rule'. It is unclear whether handles bound inside an IF condition stay in scope for the then-block.

problems.what: 'Expel / remove a member from the office'
problems.workaround: Used contain.opp (두걱안 = exclude) with AGENT manager, THEME member and FROM office.

problems.what: Heading with a role inside ('contract about a shared office'). HEAD takes a bare phrase
problems.workaround: Bracketed it: 꺄 ( 으븐 스 메훌욱 ... ), following the 'About, inside a phrase' convention.

problems.what: Clock times: 'the period from 9:00 to 12:00 on every day'
problems.workaround: Wrote ( period FROM 9 hour TO 12 hour ) OF ALL day. '9 hour' reads as a duration of nine hours, not nine o'clock; the sheet has no convention for time of day (the only example is 'before REL 9').

problems.what: 'within N days' / 'within one month' / 'within 14 days after the decision' (deadline windows)
problems.workaround: Used WHEN inside REL 1 month, and WHEN inside REL ( 14 day KIND ( next REL THAT decide.made ) ). Not sure 'inside' is meant for time, and 'N days after X' has no stated pattern (only 'ago REL 2 day' and 'before REL x').

problems.what: Define ordinary roles ('member', 'guest') as the three contract terms
problems.workaround: Roots member/guest exist with their own senses (and member is type R), and the sheet does not say whether DEFINE may redefine an existing root, so I burned three spare words (member, guest, quiet time) instead. A reader gets opaque spare forms for very ordinary notions.

problems.what: 'penalty / fine' and 'deadline'
problems.workaround: Used punish.made for the penalty (by rule it could also read as 'the one punished'); deadlines expressed only as MUST ... WHEN before REL date, no noun.

problems.what: 'rent' as a noun (the money owed)
problems.workaround: price OF rent (rent is an act root; rent.made would be the rented thing).

problems.what: 'the last person to leave'
problems.workaround: person KIND { leave KIND ( MOST late ) AGENT SELF } using KIND-after-predicate as manner; unsure whether a bracketed degree phrase is allowed as a manner modifier, and there is no word for 'last' (end is relational).

problems.what: Bind a handle to a participant introduced inside an IF condition or inside a modifier block and reuse it in the consequent / a sibling phrase (generic 'a member A ... then A must')
problems.workaround: Used NAMED inside the condition block and inside a KIND block (sentences 12, 13, 16) and the handle afterwards. The sheet does not say whether a handle bound under IF is a bound variable or a specific individual, nor its scope.

problems.what: 'a rule applies / does not apply' and 'two rules contradict each other'
problems.workaround: apply THEME rule with no AGENT (passive-like), and consistent.opp REL MUTUAL THEME 2 rule. Unclear whether MUTUAL may fill a REL slot, and whether STEP 7 can be the THEME of 'apply' to mean 'rule 7'.

problems.what: 'the noun of a derived word': 'the contradiction still exists' (consistent.opp + ness)
problems.workaround: Sheet does not say whether suffixes stack, so I repeated the full clause 'STILL contradict REL MUTUAL THEME THAT 2 rule'.

problems.what: 'the right to invite guests'
problems.workaround: ( entitlement ABOUT invite ) — dropped 'guests' because an act head with its object inside a bracketed role phrase got too nested.

problems.what: An exception to a numbered rule
problems.workaround: RULE CONTRAST 7 IF { urgent THEME call } { NOT apply THEME STEP 7 }. There is an 'exception' root (REL) and an EXCEPT role, but no relation particle for 'exception to sentence N'; CONTRAST was the closest.

problems.what: 'only if a majority agrees may a rule be changed'
problems.workaround: Turned it into the contrapositive: IF { NOT agree AGENT MAJOR member } { NOT MAY change THEME ANY rule }, since 'only if' has no construction (ONLY before IF is not covered).

problems.what: Month name 'January'
problems.workaround: NAME + letter-table loan; every block of the loan is also a particle form (주 테 우 가), which is legal as one word but hard to read and easy to mis-space.

problems.what: 'acceleration' (and 'accelerate/decelerate')
problems.workaround: Bound a handle with DEFINE to 'rate REL ( change OF ( speed OF A ) )' and used 'speed decreases SPAN 10 «m/s» PER second'

problems.what: 'up / upward / down / downward' as directions
problems.workaround: Used the relational root 'above' and 'above.opp' bare, without a REL term, as a TO-goal ('TO above') and as 'direction KIND above.opp'; unclear whether a relational root may stand without REL

problems.what: 'Earth' the planet
problems.workaround: Used the root 'world' (the earth and all on it)

problems.what: 'opposite' (force opposite to the motion), 'initial' (initial speed), 'square' as an operation (t squared)
problems.workaround: Said gravity pulls the ball 'TO above.opp' while it rises; bound initial speed to a handle in the throw sentence; wrote multiply FIRST t SECOND t

problems.what: Decimal numbers such as 9.8 or 1.6 and negative numbers such as -10; the sheet only says 'digits' and ' . ' ends a sentence
problems.workaround: Rounded g to AROUND 10 to avoid decimals; put «1.6 m/s^2» and «-10 m/s» wholly inside notation brackets; elsewhere wrote the negative as add.opp FIRST 0 SECOND B

problems.what: Mixing slot-style logic expressions with role clauses and attaching units to a computed value; whether 'EQUAL THEME x THAN ( divide FIRST 20 SECOND 10 )' followed by a unit is allowed
problems.workaround: Stated the bare computation first, then restated with ANDC RESTATE 'EQUAL THEME x THAN AROUND 2 «s»'

problems.what: Giving a formula both natively and in conventional symbols in one sentence, and tying native handles to the symbols v0, g, t, h (DEFINE handle BE «name» would read as reassigning the handle)
problems.workaround: Wrote each formula twice: once as a logic expression with handles, once as 'EQUAL THEME formula OF V THAN «v = v0 - g*t»'; the symbol-to-handle mapping is left implicit

problems.what: A handle bound to a moment (the instant of the highest point) reused as a numeric time value in formulas
problems.workaround: Used the same handle for both the moment and its time value

problems.what: 'the speed/height at time t' as a noun phrase (a WHEN role inside a phrase)
problems.workaround: Defined handles simply as 'speed OF A' and 'height OF A KIND { measured FROM point OF throw }' and left the time dependence to the formulas

problems.what: 'magnitude of the velocity' and sign conventions (velocity positive upward)
problems.workaround: 'big.ness OF V' for magnitude; a separate sentence 'positive THEME V WHEN { rise THEME A }' ANDC 'positive.opp ... WHEN { rise.opp ... }'

problems.what: Comparison across places: 'gravity is weaker on the Moon than on Earth' and 'g on Earth is 6 times g on the Moon'
problems.workaround: Used 'AT moon THAN AT world' (THAN followed by a role particle), assuming the rule extends to AT phrases; in the 6-times sentence the AT phrases follow the THEME and may be parsed ambiguously

problems.what: Role phrase with a relational head and its own REL block: 'WHEN after { the ball leaves the hand }' and 'AT near ( surface REL world )'
problems.workaround: Wrapped in brackets: WHEN ( before.opp REL { ... } ) and AT ( near REL ( surface REL world ) ); unsure REL may take a { } block or nested bracket

problems.what: 'the ball comes back' with a non-controlling subject; 'return' is an [A] root so the ball had to be AGENT
problems.workaround: return AGENT A TO land

problems.what: Stating a time point by value ('at t = 4 s', 'at time 2*C')
problems.workaround: WHEN AROUND 4 «s» and WHEN ( multiply FIRST 2 SECOND C ), i.e. a bare quantity as a WHEN phrase

problems.what: acceleration (the acceleration due to gravity g)
problems.workaround: Defined «g» as ( rate REL ( decrease.opp-of-increase OF ( speed OF ball ) ) ): 키죽 랴 ( 뜨른안 래 ( 꺼득음 래 각 ) ). This only works for the signed velocity and is clumsy.

problems.what: velocity, meaning signed speed with a direction (up positive, down negative)
problems.workaround: Used speed (꺼득음, fast.ness) and added a RULE sentence saying «v» is positive while the ball rises and negative while it falls.

problems.what: upward, as a direction of throwing
problems.workaround: Split it into two clauses: throw THEME ball ANDC SEQUENCE rise THEME ball.

problems.what: trajectory or flight path, and 'flight time'
problems.workaround: Used ( time OF ( WHOLE travel OF ball ) ), with travel 또당 standing in for the flight.

problems.what: air resistance / drag
problems.workaround: ASSUMED that the air does not obstruct the ball (하 츠학 사 두룩 새 각).

problems.what: Earth, the planet
problems.workaround: Used world 버찹.

problems.what: Decimal numbers such as 9.8 and 2.04. The rules say only 'digits are written as digits', and ' . ' is the sentence end
problems.workaround: Wrote bare decimals like 9.8 (no spaces), hoping the parser does not read the dot as a sentence end.

problems.what: Negative quantities such as v = -9.4 m/s. It is not clear whether a minus sign is allowed outside « »
problems.workaround: Put the whole value and unit in notation: «-9.4 m/s» and «-v0».

problems.what: Approximately equal (≈). AROUND before a number seems to fit, but it is unclear whether a «formula» NOTE number combination is valid
problems.workaround: Wrote EQUAL ... THAN «20/9.8» NOTE AROUND 2.04 «s».

problems.what: A derived step that rests on two suppositions at once (the scenario, and the no-air assumption). The rule describes UNDER with a single label
problems.workaround: Wrote 따 1 2 (UNDER 1 2), assuming several labels are allowed like after DERIVED.

problems.what: Whether a WHEN or AT role phrase placed before the first clause covers clauses joined by ANDC
problems.workaround: Repeated the WHEN block after each clause in sentence 26. In the moon sentences (35–37) I put AT moon before the predicate.

problems.what: Whether a «symbol» from notation can stand as a bare head or participant (THEME «v»), and whether a handle (곡) bound to a time point can be equated with a value («v0/g»)
problems.workaround: Used them directly, e.g. 티 새 «v» 슈 «v0 - g*t» and 티 새 곡 슈 «v0/g». The second is semantically loose.

problems.what: 'time since the throw' and 'height above the throw point' as quantities
problems.workaround: Put role phrases inside brackets: ( 고걱 서 ( 네풋 래 각 ) ) and ( 베딤음 래 각 서 ( 쿠중 래 ( 네풋 래 각 ) ) ). This is long but works.

problems.what: Comparing one quantity under two settings ('6 times higher on the Moon than on Earth')
problems.workaround: Repeated the whole phrase on both sides of THAN, each with its own AT role inside: ( 베딤음 래 각 셔 곡 세 트릿 ) 슈 ( 베딤음 래 각 셔 곡 세 버찹 ).

problems.what: Final summary: 'no formula changes on the Moon, only g changes'
problems.workaround: Wrote 하 느참 새 모 후킴 (NOT change THEME NONE formula). Because NOT scopes over NONE, this reads as a double negative ('it is not the case that no formula changes'). The intended form is 느참 새 모 후킴. This was my error; the rules on scope are clear but easy to trip over, and I was told not to revise the file.

problems.what: Conditional probability P(A | B), the core notion of the task (sensitivity = P(positive | disease), specificity, and P(disease | positive))
problems.workaround: Wrapped it as IF { B } { EQUAL THEME ( probable OF { A } ) THAN 95 percent }, and for the target I used 'probability OF { 혹 has the disease }' with the conditioning left implicit in the earlier steps. Nothing in the grammar says whether 'probability OF {clause}' is the right way to name the probability of a proposition.

problems.what: Linking a modifier to a whole clause: 'the probability that X', where X is a clause
problems.workaround: Used OF + { } block (쏘돈 래 { ... }). KIND + { } is a relative clause that needs SELF, and the rule sheet only lists blocks after role particles, not after OF, so I am not sure this is valid.

problems.what: 'sensitivity' and 'specificity' as technical terms
problems.workaround: Did not name them. I spelled out their meaning as the conditional probability sentences 3 and 4 and did not define spare words.

problems.what: 'test positive' / 'test negative' (a diagnostic result)
problems.workaround: Used positive (히혼, glossed 'greater than zero; affirming') and positive.opp for the result REL the test. I relied on the 'affirming' sense, so it may read as 'the result is greater than zero'.

problems.what: Saying 'a person who does not have the disease' inside an IF condition without NOT taking scope over an amount word
problems.workaround: Used a bare head (NOT have AGENT person NAMED 막 THEME 각), because NOT ANY person would mean 'no person'. Elsewhere I used a relative clause (person KIND { NOT have AGENT SELF THEME 각 }). The bare-head version still leaves it unclear whether NOT covers the person.

problems.what: 'Test of a particular person' (the test applied to person X)
problems.workaround: Wrote ( 닥 스 막 ), test ABOUT person, using the bracketed ABOUT-in-phrase convention. There is no role that clearly means 'the person tested'.

problems.what: Decimal numbers and arithmetic such as 0.95 × 0.02 / 0.117, including the percent sign
problems.workaround: Put all arithmetic in « » notation as WITH-phrases (소 «...»), and wrote percentages natively as number + 르님 (percent). It is unclear whether a decimal like 0.95 is legal as a bare number, since ' . ' is the sentence end.

problems.what: Discharging a supposition that was only a calculation device (an imagined group of 10000 people) without a DERIVED IF sentence
problems.workaround: Added a CLAIM that step 18 does not depend on the size of the group, then a DERIVED sentence citing the general premises plus 18 and 19. The rule sheet only describes discharge via DERIVED IF.

problems.what: Where a WITH-phrase (the arithmetic) goes in an IF sentence
problems.workaround: Put it inside the then-block, because a role phrase after both blocks has no clear attachment.

problems.what: 'Each result is either positive or negative' (exactly one of two qualities as predicate)
problems.workaround: Used a bracketed XOR of two qualities as the predicate: ( 히혼 루 히혼안 ) 새 마 베건 랴 닥. XOR is defined for phrases, and its use as a predicate is not shown in the rule sheet.

problems.what: 'People mistake the 95% figure for the answer' (confusing P(A|B) with P(B|A))
problems.workaround: Wrote 'people use 95 percent AS ( answer.made FOR step 6 )' and 'step 3 is different from step 6'. These are only approximations of 'confusing the direction of the conditional'.

problems.what: Conditional probability: 'the probability that the result is positive GIVEN that the person has the disease' (P(A|B)), and its converse
problems.workaround: probability KIND { IF {C has B} {result positive} }, i.e. the probability of an if-then clause. This reads like the probability of a material conditional, which is a different thing; I could not tell whether WHEN {…} inside the block or IF was the intended way. Both conditional probabilities in the text (sentences 13, 14, 17) depend on this guess.

problems.what: Decimal numbers such as 0.02, 0.117
problems.workaround: Wrote them in « » («0.02»). Section 1 only says 'digits' are numbers; nothing says whether a decimal point is allowed in a bare number (and ' . ' is the sentence end). I mixed bare integers (95, 1000) with « » decimals, also as arguments of logic functions (add.opp FIRST 1 SECOND «0.02»).

problems.what: 'sensitivity' and 'specificity' of a test
problems.workaround: Defined two spare words (사붕, 모민) as 'probability KIND { result of test is positive FOR a sick person }' and '... negative FOR a healthy person'. Worked, but the definition itself needs the conditional-probability construction that is missing, so I used FOR + person as a stand-in.

problems.what: 'test result' / 'a positive test result' / 'someone tests positive'
problems.workaround: result REL A with positive as predicate and the person behind FOR: 'positive THEME result REL A FOR person'. test.made was ambiguous (product vs. thing tested), and it is unclear whether FOR (beneficiary) or OF is the right way to say whose result it is.

problems.what: Percent of a group, and percent as a value: '2% of people', 'equals 95%'
problems.workaround: '2 percent OF population' and 'EQUAL ... THAN 95 percent', treating percent as a countable head. The word list gives percent as a thing but no example; I was unsure whether «%» notation was intended instead, and whether 'ALMOST/AROUND 16 percent' parses.

problems.what: Mark a long derivation as resting on two assumptions (random selection, no other evidence)
problems.workaround: Put 'UNDER 9 10' on every derived step and discharged with a final 'DERIVED 9 10 18 IF {true THEME STEP 9 ANDC true THEME STEP 10} {...}'. The rule sheet shows UNDER with one label only and shows discharge only by negation; whether UNDER takes several labels, and how to discharge two assumptions at once, is not stated.

problems.what: 'more numerous than' / 'there are far more healthy people than sick people' as a predicate
problems.workaround: MANY is only an amount word, not a predicate, so I named the two groups with handles and wrote 'group S2 is 49 times as big as group S' (49 EQUAL big).

problems.what: '19 of them' / 'of these 20 people, 19 ...' (partitive referring back)
problems.workaround: Bound a handle to the counted group ('20 person NAMED S') and then wrote '19 person OF S'. Unclear whether a handle bound to '20 person' denotes the group, and whether OF + handle is a legal partitive.

problems.what: A clause starting with a number right after a relation ('RESTATE: 49 times as big ...')
problems.workaround: The number would be read as a label, so I moved the THEME phrase in front of the predicate ('RESTATE THEME S2 49 EQUAL big THAN S'). Section 11 only covers this for replies; in general prose it forces unnatural order.

problems.what: Prior probability: 'the probability that C has the disease before the result is known'
problems.workaround: Added 'WHEN before REL { know THEME result REL A }' at clause level. It is unclear whether this attaches to the EQUAL clause or should be inside the probability's block; no word for prior/posterior.

problems.what: Binding a handle to a value inside a prose sentence and then using it in logic expressions
problems.workaround: 'probability NAMED P KIND {…}' and later '( multiply FIRST P SECOND S )'. The sheet shows NAMED for things and DEFINE handle BE expr for logic values; whether the two kinds of handle interoperate is not stated. Also unsure whether a block after 'probability KIND' needs SELF (it has no natural place for it).

problems.what: 'people confuse P(positive|sick) with P(sick|positive)'
problems.workaround: confuse is an [E] root whose THEME is the confused mind, with no slot for the two things confused; I wrote 'many people think that G equals S, but G is different REL S' and then 'S is ABOUT all sick people, G is ABOUT all people whose result is positive'.

problems.what: Read the whole word list in one pass
problems.workaround: The file exceeded the read cap, so I had to read it in two pages; no content problem, but noted.

problems.what: Look up a value in a map by key (neighbours of a node; current count of a word), and write a map entry
problems.workaround: Used undeclared library names «get» FIRST map SECOND key and «set» FIRST map SECOND key THIRD value. The sheet only defines `item FIRST list SECOND n` for positional list access and «append»; there is no map/dictionary convention at all.

problems.what: Literal for an empty map and an empty string
problems.workaround: Wrote «{}» and «""» by analogy with «[]», which is the only empty literal the sheet defines.

problems.what: Membership test 'Y is not in list V' / 'map M has key W' as a condition
problems.workaround: Used the root contain in function position: `NOT contain FIRST V SECOND Y`. The sheet says NOT may stand before a comparison, but does not say whether an ordinary root call may serve as a boolean condition or be negated.

problems.what: 'reverse' (a string) as a function name
problems.workaround: Compound ( turn KIND sequence ) plus a code-name definition BE «reverse». No root for reverse/backwards; the compound is a guess a reader may not decode without the code name.

problems.what: 'breadth-first' search
problems.workaround: ( search KIND wide ) with code name «bfs».

problems.what: String operations: iterate over the characters of a string, and concatenate a character in front of a string
problems.workaround: Used EACH handle IN string, assuming it iterates characters, and the root join as `join FIRST char SECOND string` for concatenation. Neither is defined in the logic section (there is also no word for 'character'/'string'; I avoided needing them by using handles only).

problems.what: A queue (remove the first item of a list / pop) for the classic BFS formulation
problems.workaround: Rewrote BFS level by level with a frontier list and a next-frontier list, so no dequeue operation was needed. There is no convention for removing or slicing list items.

problems.what: Whether handles bound as function parameters / by DEFINE inside logic stay usable as referents in the following prose
problems.workaround: Assumed yes (section 11: handles stay bound for the whole text) and used the BFS handles for start node, target, visited list, frontier and distance in the explanation; used different handles in the other two functions to avoid rebinding them.

problems.what: 'The function returns nothing' in a prose sentence
problems.workaround: RETURN is a structure particle for logic blocks, not a predicate, so I wrote `give AGENT ( search KIND wide ) THEME EMPTY`.

problems.what: 'visits nearer nodes before farther ones' (before + a clause)
problems.workaround: REL is a linker and the sheet does not say it can take a { } block, so I wrote two clauses joined by ANDC SEQUENCE: visits all nodes at distance 1, and then all nodes at distance 2 (loses the general 'layer by layer' statement).

problems.what: 'the length of the shortest path from S to T' and 'distance from S to the node'
problems.workaround: Put role phrases inside brackets after a head: ( long.ness OF road KIND ( MOST short ) FROM S TO T ) and ( near.ness FROM S TO SELF ). Because every modifier attaches to the head, 'shortest' modifies length rather than path; and the bracket-with-roles convention is only shown for ABOUT, so FROM/TO there is an extrapolation. 'road' stands in for graph path; 'near.ness' for edge-count distance.

problems.what: Two consecutive IF statements and nested EACH inside an EACH block within a function body
problems.workaround: Separated statements with ` . ` and nested the blocks directly, following the examples; the sheet never shows an EACH directly inside another EACH's block or a RETURN inside nested loops, so I assumed it exits the whole function.

problems.what: Look up a value by key in a map/dictionary (graph[node] -> neighbour list). The logic section defines item FIRST list SECOND n only for list positions.
problems.workaround: Used the root 'assign' (꾸쿵, noun: mapping) as a function: ( 꾸쿵 오 graph 요 node ), and added a RULE sentence saying that for each node this equals the list of its neighbours.

problems.what: Build or update a map (word -> count): an empty-map literal and assignment to a map entry. DEFINE only assigns to a handle, and only «[]» and «append» exist for lists.
problems.workaround: Kept two parallel lists (words and counts) and rebuilt the whole counts list element by element to increment one count.

problems.what: Return two values or a tuple/pair from a function (the word list and its counts).
problems.workaround: Returned ( 거깁 오 words 요 counts ), using the relational root 'pair' as a function. Its meaning as a constructor is not defined anywhere.

problems.what: A membership test ('x in list') and a boolean NOT applied to a function result. The rules only allow NOT before a comparison.
problems.workaround: Defined my own function ( 두걱 라 째즛 ) 'contain KIND item' that returns YES/NO, and tested it with EQUAL ... SECOND NO.

problems.what: Remove the front of a queue (pop), plus negative numbers such as -1 as a not-found sentinel.
problems.workaround: Never removed anything: walked the queue with an index handle, and used count(list) as the not-found sentinel.

problems.what: 'reverse' (reverse a string/order), 'string' (character string), and an empty-string literal.
problems.workaround: Defined the function under spare word 모민 and gave it the code name «reverse». Treated the string as indexable with item/count, wrote the empty string as «""» and concatenation as ( 므듭 = join ). 'add' is for numbers only, and 'join' as string concatenation is my own stretch.

problems.what: 'breadth' / 'breadth-first', 'graph edge', 'path length' / 'distance in a graph', 'queue empty'.
problems.workaround: Wrote ( 푸증 라 삐쿰음 ) 'search KIND width' for BFS, near.ness ( 수폭음 서 x 샤 y ) for distance, road/path 어킁 for path, 써깃 'queue' for the queue, and full.opp for empty. I left edges out entirely.

problems.what: Whether a function's code name can be given by DEFINE spare BE «identifier», and whether a spare word can be bound directly as a function name with FIRST slots.
problems.workaround: Did both: 까 모민 오 북 체 {...} followed by 까 모민 체 «reverse».

problems.what: Saying 'returns X' in prose. RETURN (츄) is a logic particle, not a root that can be a predicate.
problems.workaround: Used 'the result of the search is X': 티 새 ( 베건 랴 search ) 슈 X.

problems.what: 'the search processes nodes in order of increasing distance' (the reason BFS finds the shortest path)
problems.workaround: Wrote 'always takes, in a more early manner, nodes having distance KIND (MORE small)': 짜 네절 라 ( 툐 라둣 ) ... 새 으점 레 ( 수폭음 라 ( 툐 떠못안 ) ). The comparison base is left implicit.

problems.what: Whether WHILE {cond} {block} may be the body of an ordinary CLAIM sentence in prose, not only inside logic code. The spec allows that explicitly only for EACH.
problems.workaround: Used it anyway in explanation sentence 2: 겨 도 1 추 { ... } { ... } .

problems.what: 'severity' with levels high / medium / low
problems.workaround: Used importance as the scale: VERY important (high), plain important (medium), SLIGHT important (low). The scale is never stated explicitly, and 'medium' is just the bare quality.

problems.what: 'line of code' / 'line number'
problems.workaround: 애컨 (line: long thin mark or row) with ORD, e.g. 너 3 애컨 래 각 (ORD 3 line OF the function). I am not sure the meaning stretches that far.

problems.what: 'raise / throw an exception', 'produce an error'
problems.workaround: Used cause with the code as AGENT and the error as THEME (파킨 사 «xs[i]» 새 체낫 ...), and 'appear' (뻬슨) for an error showing up. 'Fails with error X' became fail WITH error KIND «...».

problems.what: 'fix' as a noun (the proposed change)
problems.workaround: Wrote each fix as a PROPOSE sentence: replace THEME new SWAP old, or put THEME «code» AT before REL line 2. For 'after fixing problem 1' I used ( 테벗 래 낙 ), i.e. repair OF the problem, which is a stretch because repair means 'make work again'.

problems.what: 'by hand / manually', 'built-in function', 'iterate over indices'
problems.workaround: 'loop HAVING index' (히믹 레 스송). I dropped 'by hand' and 'built-in' and said only that «sum(xs)» equals the sum of all items.

problems.what: 'argument / input passed to a function' (fails when given an empty list)
problems.workaround: WHEN { get AGENT the-function THEME list KIND full.opp }, using 'get' for receiving an argument.

problems.what: Whether a bare « » notation can be a phrase head or an AGENT (e.g. «range(len(xs) + 1)» as the AGENT of contain, «xs» as OF-owner), and whether KIND «...» is allowed without NAME for an error message
problems.workaround: Used « » directly as heads and after KIND without NAME. I reserved NAME for the function name «average».

problems.what: Where a WHEN phrase goes in an IF sentence so that it applies only to the then-clause
problems.workaround: Put the WHEN phrase inside the then-block, before the predicate (sentence 16).

problems.what: 'Neither error message names the real cause (the empty list)'
problems.workaround: NOT say AGENT ( «IndexError» OR «ZeroDivisionError» ) THEME ( cause REL error ) NOTE ( list KIND full.opp ). It relies on NOT over OR to mean 'neither', and on NOTE meaning 'namely'.

problems.what: Showing the full corrected function as multi-line code
problems.workaround: Gave it as separate fixes: a single-line guard «if not xs: raise ValueError(...)» inserted before line 2, and «return sum(xs) / len(xs)» in place of lines 2 to 5. A closing IF/then/else sentence states the resulting behaviour.

problems.what: 'severity' (high / low severity of a problem)
problems.workaround: Used the quality 'important' with degree particles: VERY important / SLIGHT important THEME ORD n problem. 'serious' exists but is glossed 'earnest, not joking', so it did not fit.

problems.what: 'line 3' / 'problem 1' as a numbered noun inside a clause. The sheet only shows a number after the head in HEAD sentences ('HEAD task 2') and with STEP; phrase grammar has no slot for a trailing number.
problems.workaround: Used ORD: 'ORD 3 line', 'ORD 1 problem', and 'ORD 2 UPTO 4 line' for a line range.

problems.what: 'line of code' - the only 'line' root is glossed 'long thin mark or row'
problems.workaround: Used that root (line) anyway and attached the quoted code with NOTE «...».

problems.what: Attaching a quoted identifier or code fragment to a noun: is it 'function KIND NAME «average»', 'function KIND «average»', or 'function NOTE «...»'? Whether bare « » can be a participant or modifier outside logic is not stated; only 'KIND NAME «User-Agent»' and logic values are shown.
problems.workaround: Used 'KIND NAME «x»' for identifiers (average, xs, i, sum, IndexError), 'expression KIND «...»' for code fragments, and 'NOTE «...»' for whole code lines and the exact error message.

problems.what: 'raise / throw an exception' and 'exception' (Python sense)
problems.workaround: Said 'a message of kind error NOTE «IndexError: ...» appears' and 'the expression fails'; for the fix, put the raise statement entirely inside « ».

problems.what: 'replace X with Y' - the root 'replace' does not say which role holds the old vs the new thing
problems.workaround: Used 'use THEME new SWAP old' instead of the replace root.

problems.what: 'division by zero is impossible' / 'divide by 0' in prose - divide is a logic function with FIRST/SECOND slots, and leaving FIRST out is not covered
problems.workaround: Wrote CAUSE { NOT CAN divide WITH 0 } using the WITH role for the divisor.

problems.what: 'add a check at the start of the function' - 'add' is glossed as arithmetic only, and 'guard clause' has no word
problems.workaround: Used 'put AT end.opp REL function THEME check NOTE «code»'.

problems.what: 'the largest valid index of the list' needs three modifiers on one head
problems.workaround: Stacked them flat: index OF B KIND valid KIND ( MOST big ); unsure the reader will take MOST big as a superlative over the valid indices.

problems.what: 'idiomatic / unnecessary / redundant' for the third problem (index loop where sum() suffices)
problems.workaround: Said 'the function does not need a loop HAVING index' and 'if the code is longer, a defect is more probable'.

problems.what: DERIVED followed by labels and then a relation that takes its own label (e.g. 'DERIVED 4 EXPLAIN 3'): the digits run together and it is not stated how the reader splits them, only the example 'DERIVED 1 UNDER 1'.
problems.workaround: Wrote the labels, then the relation particle, then its label, following that example.

problems.what: Logical/metaphysical necessity ('identity is necessarily transitive', 'it must be that x = y'), distinct from obligation
problems.workaround: Used MUST (카, glossed 'required') inside the then-block of an IF, plus CERTAIN in the header; the reader may take it as deontic. There is no 'necessarily' particle and no root for 'necessary'.

problems.what: Put a modal or UNREAL over a whole IF construction ('necessarily, if A then B'; 'it would be that if...')
problems.workaround: Sheet says pre-predicate particles stand before the predicate, but does not say whether they may stand before IF. I put MUST/UNREAL inside each block separately (UNREAL repeated in both condition and consequence).

problems.what: 'sufficient' / 'necessary condition' (memories are not sufficient for identity)
problems.workaround: ENOUGH is only a degree particle needing a predicate, so I wrote 'same memories do not imply same identity' with imply REL, and 'identity needs continuity' with need.

problems.what: 'objection' and 'reply' as nouns for a heading
problems.workaround: Heading 'section 3 NOTE ( disagree.opp-form AND answer )', i.e. the act roots disagree and answer as heads; the objection itself is carried only by the REBUT relation.

problems.what: Argue for a claim and then against it without asserting both sides myself
problems.workaround: No opener for 'one side argues'. ASSUMED+UNDER would force every step into a supposition, so I invented two story persons (supporter, rejecter) and put each side's sentences under BY with CLAIM/DERIVED. Whether DERIVED/ASSUMED/UNDER inside BY turns are checked as that speaker's commitments is not stated.

problems.what: Mark a block of STORY sentences as 'a thought experiment'
problems.workaround: Attached 'NOTE experiment KIND think' to the last phrase of the first story sentence; it formally attaches to the head 'machine/world' phrase, not to the sentence. A heading inside the section would have broken the section structure.

problems.what: 'memories' as countable contents (all of a person's memories)
problems.workaround: Word list gives memory = remember.ness (abstract state); I built remember.made by rule for 'things remembered'. Unsure the reader distinguishes them.

problems.what: 'difference' / 'whether B differs from A'; also 'whether' clauses in general (identity depends on whether another copy exists)
problems.workaround: Used a bare block { different REL A THEME B } as THEME of 'show', and for 'depends on whether X exists' used a nominalised 'depend REL ( exist OF other copy.made )' because REL is a linker and the sheet does not say it may take a { } block.

problems.what: Say 'B thinks that B itself is A' with a reflexive
problems.workaround: SELF outside a KIND block means the AGENT of its own clause, and the inner clause (EQUAL THEME ... THAN ...) has no AGENT, so I repeated the handle instead.

problems.what: State numeric confidence ('about 80% sure the claim is false')
problems.workaround: Wrote LIKELY «0.8» before NOT true. The sheet says a number in « » may follow a strength but does not say whether it is a probability, nor whether it scopes over the following NOT.

problems.what: Refer to a range of earlier sentences as one thing ('steps 29 to 31 are stronger than steps 27 to 28')
problems.workaround: Wrote ( STEP 29 UPTO 31 ) with UPTO after a STEP label; the sheet lists UPTO for 'numbers or labels' but gives no example with STEP.

problems.what: Predicate 'is still the same person' (SAME + thing as predicate)
problems.workaround: Avoided it; wrote 'the identity of the person does not change' and used EQUAL THEME x THAN y for identity throughout. Unclear whether an amount word like SAME may open a predicate phrase without brackets.

problems.what: Earth, Mars
problems.workaround: 'world' for Earth; 'planet KIND NAME' + letter-table loan for Mars.

problems.what: 'One and the same thing cannot die while it stays alive'
problems.workaround: 'NOT CAN die THEME ANY thing ALONG { alive THEME SAME thing }' — relies on SAME thing picking up the ANY thing of the outer clause, which the sheet does not guarantee (a binding handle on an ANY phrase is not described).

problems.what: A claim whose content is a conditional, attached to the noun 'claim' and given a handle
problems.workaround: Wrote 'claim.made NAMED D KIND { IF {..} {..} }'. KIND + block is defined as a relative clause with SELF; using it as a content clause ('the claim that ...') is only supported by the gloss 'content' on KIND.

problems.what: 'a copy of person X': the original that a copy was made from
problems.workaround: copy.made OF X (떠링엄 래 각). 'copy' is not a relational [R] root, so it cannot take REL, and OF officially means 'owner or whole', which is the wrong relation.

problems.what: Logical or metaphysical necessity ('necessarily', 'must be the case')
problems.workaround: 'impossible that (A and not B)' with possible.opp (배텃안) in sentence 12, and MUST (카) in sentence 23. MUST is glossed as 'required', which reads as an obligation, not a necessity.

problems.what: Presenting an argument I do not endorse (arguing the 'for' side and then the 'against' side). No opener means 'argued for the sake of debate'.
problems.workaround: Gave each side to a hypothetical speaker using BY with a bound phrase (채 쁘칸 차 학 라 {support AGENT SELF THEME D}), so that CLAIM and DERIVED are in that speaker's voice.

problems.what: 'in every possible case / in all possible worlds' as a participant role
problems.workaround: AT ALL case KIND possible (세 마 씨콥 라 배텃). AT is defined as a place.

problems.what: A heading 'reasons against D', i.e. reasons for 'D is false'. It is unclear whether REL can take a { } block.
problems.workaround: reason REL ( true.opp OF D ), using falsity as a quality head.

problems.what: The scope of handles bound by EACH (각, 낙 inside the definition of the claim). Section 11 says handles stay bound for the whole text, which conflicts with their use as loop variables.
problems.workaround: Used fresh handles (독, 목, 복, 곡, 녹, 족) everywhere else so that nothing could clash.

problems.what: Adding a further supposed detail inside an existing supposition (the copies live in different cities)
problems.workaround: ASSUMED UNDER 16 (게 따 16 ...). The sheet only shows UNDER with DERIVED, so I am not sure an ASSUMED step may itself be marked UNDER.

problems.what: Discharging a reductio. The supposition was the duplication scenario, but the thing refuted is D (sentence 1).
problems.workaround: A DERIVED IF sentence (22): 'if the machine made 복, D is false'. Then a separate premise that a claim about identity must hold in every possible case, plus the possibility claim (15), to conclude that D is false.

problems.what: 'might' (epistemic possibility) inside a counterfactual consequent
problems.workaround: Strength particles go only in the sentence header, so I used UNREAL + CAN (헤 커) inside the block.

problems.what: 'the same person as' (identity of persons over time)
problems.workaround: EQUAL alone as the predicate ('is identical to'), together with identity OF X (빼눙 래 X). There is no separate notion of personal sameness as opposed to qualitative sameness.

problems.what: Which role the person being asked takes with 'ask' (투빈)
problems.workaround: Asker as AGENT, the person asked as TO, and the topic with ABOUT.

problems.what: 'what matters to X' / 'the things that are important to X'
problems.workaround: MANY thing KIND { important FOR X } (먀 디훅 라 { 초는 수 독 }).

problems.what: Write a full calendar date: 14 June 1919, and a bare year (1948, 1927).
problems.workaround: Wrote 'ORD 14 day OF ( month KIND NAME june OF year 1919 )' and 'WHEN year 1948'. The sheet only shows 'WHEN NAME ~friday'; whether a number may follow the head 'year' (as in 'HEAD task 2') and whether a month name goes bare or after KIND is not stated.

problems.what: non-stop (a flight without landing on the way); also 'land' as a verb and 'take off'
problems.workaround: 'WITH NONE stay AT land' for non-stop; 'BEGIN fly' for take off; 'STOP fly AT ...' for land.

problems.what: ocean / the proper name Atlantic Ocean; bog
problems.workaround: 'sea KIND NAME ~atlantic'; bog = 'land KIND wet KIND hard.opp' plus 'mud'.

problems.what: pilot and navigator as nouns
problems.workaround: Avoided the nouns: 'A drove D and B measured the position of D and the direction of D'.

problems.what: generator, exhaust pipe, newspaper, knighthood, bomber
problems.workaround: 'make.tool KIND electricity', 'pipe OF engine', 'paper KIND news', 'rank KIND honour' given by the king, 'D was made for war'. All readable but vague; knighthood especially loses its meaning.

problems.what: 'X seemed (to A) to be Y' / 'A mistook the bog for a firm field': the root seem [E] has no documented slot for what the thing seems to be.
problems.workaround: 'A thought that { ( field KIND solid ) THEME THAT land }'.

problems.what: Mark certainty about an earlier sentence ('I am not sure sentence 17 is true'). Unclear whether 'sure' [Q] takes the person as THEME and the matter as ABOUT.
problems.workaround: 'CLAIM ABOUT STEP 17 sure.opp THEME ME', and a closing pair of sentences listing what I am sure / unsure about.

problems.what: Join two named people each with its own handle inside one AND group, and attach OF to a bracketed AND group.
